edition.locus: Eusebius HE 5.1.15-16 (the slander believed; wrath on four)

source_text: Ταῦτα δὲ φημισθέντα, πάντες ἀπεθηριώθησαν εἰς ἡμᾶς, ὥστε καὶ εἴ τινες τὸ πρότερον δι᾽ οἰκειότητα ἐμετρίαζον, τότε μεγάλως ἐχαλέπαινον καὶ διεπρίοντο ἐφ᾽ ἡμῖν· ἐπληροῦτο δὲ τὸ ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν εἰρημένον ὅτι ἐλεύσεται καιρὸς ἐν ᾧ πᾶς ὁ ἀποκτείνας ὑμᾶς δόξει λατρείαν προσφέρειν τῷ θεῷ. Ἐνταῦθα λοιπὸν ὑπεράνω πάσης ἐξηγήσεως ὑπέμενον κολάσεις οἱ ἅγιοι μάρτυρες, φιλοτιμουμένου τοῦ σατανᾶ κἂν ἐξ ἐκείνων ῥηθῆναί τι τῶν βλασφήμων· ὑπερβεβλημένως δὲ ἐνέσκηψεν ἡ ὀργὴ πᾶσα καὶ ὄχλου καὶ ἡγεμόνος καὶ στρατιωτῶν εἰς Σάγκτον τὸν διάκονον ἀπὸ Βιέννης καὶ εἰς Μάτουρον, νεοφώτιστον μέν, ἀλλὰ γενναῖον ἀγωνιστήν, καὶ εἰς Ἄτταλον Περγαμηνὸν τῷ γένει, στῦλον καὶ ἑδραίωμα τῶν ἐνταῦθα ἀεὶ γεγονότα, καὶ εἰς Βλανδῖναν, δι᾽ ἧς ἐπέδειξεν ὁ Χριστὸς ὅτι τὰ παρὰ ἀνθρώποις εὐτελῆ καὶ ἀειδῆ καὶ εὐκαταφρόνητα φαινόμενα μεγάλης καταξιοῦται παρὰ θεῷ δόξης διὰ τὴν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀγάπην τὴν ἐν δυνάμει δεικνυμένην καὶ μὴ ἐν εἴδει καυχωμένην.
pass_a_gloss: These things having been said, all were made beast-like against us, so that even if some beforehand through acquaintance used to be moderate, then they raged greatly and were sawn-asunder with anger at us; and there was being fulfilled the thing spoken by our Lord that a time will come in which everyone killing you will think to be offering worship to God. Then henceforth beyond all description kept enduring punishments the holy martyrs, with Satan eagerly contending that even from among them might be spoken something of the blasphemous things; but exceedingly there rushed upon Sanctus the deacon from Vienne and upon Maturus, newly-enlightened but noble fighter, and upon Attalus Pergamene by birth, who had always been pillar and foundation-stay of those here, and upon Blandina — through whom Christ showed that the things among men appearing cheap and unshapely and easily despised are counted worthy of great glory before God through the love toward him shown in power and not boasting in outward form — all wrath both of crowd and of governor and of soldiers.
pass_b_english: When these charges were proclaimed, everyone turned savage against us, so that even those who before had shown restraint because they knew us now raged violently and were convulsed with fury against us. And so what was spoken by our Lord was fulfilled, that a time is coming when everyone who kills you will think he is offering worship to God (John 16:2).

From that point on the holy martyrs endured tortures beyond all telling, while Satan strove eagerly that even from their lips some blasphemous word might be uttered. And the full fury of the crowd and the governor and the soldiers fell with extraordinary violence upon Sanctus the deacon from Vienne, and upon Maturus, a newly baptized man but a noble fighter, and upon Attalus, Pergamene by birth, who had always been a pillar and bulwark of those here, and upon Blandina, through whom Christ showed that what seems among men cheap and unsightly and contemptible is counted worthy of great glory before God through love for him, a love shown in power and not boasting in outward show.

choices.why: passive aorist with εἰς expresses hostile change of disposition toward us, not literal metamorphosis into animals
paired architectural metaphor for a stabilizing supporter of the local community, with ἑδραίωμα as fixed support rather than abstract steadfastness

choices.term: τὴν ἐν δυνάμει δεικνυμένην καὶ μὴ ἐν εἴδει καυχωμένην
choices.english: shown in power and not boasting in outward show
choices.why: contrast is between δύναμις as effective endurance and εἶδος as mere appearance; καυχωμένην is boastful display, not simple pride
rejected: revealed in virtue and not glorying in form
